text:
sam: FYI nightly job `model-refresh+bench-cleanup` failed on prod-nightly-01 at ~03:10 UTC, CI marked red. Seems tied to the cleanup step hitting disk pressure.

nightly-bot: job model-refresh/2026-03-16 failed (exit=137) — logs: /var/log/nightly/2026-03-16/cleanup.log

maya: ugh. any obvious error lines in the log? :eyes:

sam: quick tail from the node: 
```
OutOfMemoryError: write failed: No space left on device
rm: cannot remove '/tmp/bench-cache/*': Device or resource busy
[cleanup] exit status 137
```

cheng: 137 usually OOM or SIGKILL. but "No space left" is disk. can you `df -h` on prod-nightly-01?

sam: df -h output (short): 
```
/dev/nvme0n1p1  95G  94G  1G  99% /
tmpfs           62G   59G  3G  96% /dev/shm
```

leo: root is nearly full. looks like the bench artifacts didn't rotate. PR that changed temp dir in build-tools might have broken cleanup retention (PR #3472).

maya: @leo can you do a manual rerun once we free up space? we should avoid noisy reruns if it's just disk constraints.

leo: will free ~20GB by nuking old bench artifacts in /var/artifacts/nightly (I have a safe list). Rerun after cleanup.

sam: doing `sudo rm -rf /var/artifacts/nightly/2026-02-*` now.

(5m later)

sam: cleanup cleared ~28GB, root now 82% used. kicked off manual rerun: `./scripts/nightly-run --job model-refresh --node prod-nightly-01 --rerun`

nightly-bot: rerun started (run id 2026-03-16-487).

(10m)

nightly-bot: rerun completed — model-refresh succeeded, bench-cleanup still failed (exit=2). Logs: /var/log/nightly/2026-03-16/cleanup-rerun.log

maya: bench-cleanup exit=2 is different. can you paste the last 20 lines of that log?

sam: last lines: 
```
INFO: started cleanup pass 1
WARN: file lock timeout on /tmp/bench-cache/index.lock
ERROR: could not remove /tmp/bench-cache/large_hash_12345: Device or resource busy
INFO: fallback: move to /var/artifacts/stuck/2026-03-16
ERROR: move failed: cross-device link
cleanup exit 2
```

cheng: cross-device link + device busy suggests some process still holding files in /tmp/bench-cache (maybe a docker volume mount). `lsof +D /tmp/bench-cache` on node?

leo: i ran lsof: found PID 3321 (runner-daemon) holding a handle. runner-daemon restarts frequently after PR #3500 changed its temp dir. Might be a timing window where it reclaims files slowly.

maya: ok — plans: 1) add a pre-clean check to kill/stop runner-daemon gracefully before cleanup; 2) add root disk alert to prevent nightly runs when >90% used; 3) revert PR #3472 or patch retention logic.

sam: agree. i'll open a quick ticket and a rollback PR for #3472. tagging @oncall for FYI.

leo: i can open the patch to stop runner-daemon before cleanup (will send a small change in the job wrapper).

cheng: for immediate CI health, we should mark the bench-cleanup task as non-blocking for the model-refresh job so deploys aren't blocked by cleanup flakiness. can we flip that in the job graph?

maya: yes, set cleanup to best-effort and gate model index publish on model-refresh success only. i'll update the job graph and add an integration test for file-handle contention.

sam: created ticket INF-1298 (rollback temp-dir PR + add retention + non-blocking cleanup) and PR #3525 (job graph change) in the ops repo.

leo: created PR #3526 (stop runner-daemon before cleanup) and set it to draft — requesting quick review from @cheng.

cheng: reviewing now. small nit on signal handling, but lgtm otherwise. will merge after CI passes. :thumbsup:

maya: adding an alert runbook step: if nightly fails with "No space left", page @eng-oncall and escalate to infra to free space or fail fast.

sam: thanks all. next steps: merge #3526, merge job-graph change, roll out retention patch, then re-enable full blocking behavior. leaving thread open for any fallout. :white_check_mark:
